meta.what: Every exploration zone (EZ) proposed in the abstracts of NASA's First Landing Site/Exploration Zone Workshop for Human Missions to the Surface of Mars, with the position each abstract states, checked against the organisers' map and table.

meeting.name: First Landing Site/Exploration Zone Workshop for Human Missions to the Surface of Mars
meeting.place_and_dates: Lunar and Planetary Institute, Houston, Texas, 27-30 October 2015
meeting.meeting_pages: https://www.hou.usra.edu/meetings/explorationzone2015/ (HTML pages answer automated requests with a challenge page, so the program PDF was used)

how_positions_were_taken: Each position is copied from the abstract's own words (text, table or figure caption), read with pdftotext from the saved PDF; position_as_written keeps those words.

Readers drafted the records; the merge step re-opened every saved PDF, found each quoted phrase and re-checked every number, sign and conversion. Abstracts with no reader record in the merge input (1002, 1011, 1015, 1018, 1021, 1024, 1028, 1029, 1031, 1035, 1045, 1047, 1053, 1056, and the cut-off record of 1027) were read in full in the merge step.
Where the text layer is split across two columns (1020, 1046) or uses Symbol-font glyphs for the degree and minus signs (1028), the quote was put together by hand and checked against the text.
Degrees-minutes-seconds were converted to decimal degrees; west longitudes were converted with east = 360 - west.
lat and lon_east_360 are null when the abstract does not state both. Readings from figures and from the NASA map are kept apart from them, in note and official_check.
Region checks use the USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature (planetocentric, east 0-360) as an outside cross-check only; gazetteer values never replace a stated position.

conventions.convention_field: How the abstract wrote its position (east 0-360, east -180 to 180, west, signed values with or without letters, or 'not stated').
conventions.note_on_written_conventions: Several abstracts write south latitudes as negative north values (for example '-37.2°N'); 1054 gives signed values with no convention at all.
conventions.position_kind_field: centre of the zone, landing site, position of the zone (not called the centre), centre of a named crater the zone covers, midpoint of a stated box, latitude only, or not stated.
conventions.same_as_field: Other zones, or sites the project already has, whose centres lie less than 200 km away (zones are about 100 km in radius). 'same place' means less than 50 km apart.
conventions.official_check_field: Position of the zone circle on the NASA map (v10 vector PDF; v12 JPG for the two circles only on v12), the latitude in Appendix D of the NTRS paper, and each difference of more than 1 degree.

counts.organisers_statement: NASA Final Workshop Statement: 'A total of 47 EZs were proposed in 45 abstracts submitted to the Workshop. Presentations for 44 of these 45 abstracts were made during the Workshop.'
counts.why_49_not_47: The abstracts give 49 zones in 47 abstracts, two more zones and two more abstracts than the organisers' 47 in 45. The NASA agenda (v11) has 44 EZ talks, and those 44 abstracts hold 46 zones. Two abstracts propose a zone but have no EZ talk: 1006 (Valles Marineris mouth; on the map, filed by NASA as a poster) and 1056 (Tempe Terra; on the map, not in the LPI program). 1049 (Holden crater) was a poster and is not on the map or in Appendix D. The organisers' 45 abstracts are most likely the 44 talks plus one of 1006 or 1056, which gives 47 zones. No source says which one; this is an inference, not confirmed.

official_sources_compared.nasa_map_v10: 'Potential Exploration Zones for Human Missions to the Surface of Mars', NASA Mars Program Office, version 10 vector PDF, https://www3.nasa.gov/sites/default/files/atoms/files/exploration-zone-map-v10.pdf. Mercator projection, 180 E to 180 E, 57 S to 57 N. Circle centres were taken from the vector paths and converted with the map's own graticule (6.721 pt per degree; equator at y = 694.3 pt), good to about ±0.05 degree. 44 circles carry 46 number labels (one circle reads '20, 22, 40').
official_sources_compared.nasa_map_v12: Version 12 (16 Oct 2015), JPG 5400 x 2700, https://www3.nasa.gov/sites/default/files/thumbnails/image/map-of-proposed-exploration-zones.jpg. Same layout as v10 plus two circles, both printed '18': one beside 'Amazonis Planitia' (fits abstract 1018) and one beside 'Hills Zephyria Planum' (fits abstract 1016, so its '18' is a misprint for '16'). Legend: circle numbers 'correspond to the abstract submission #'.
official_sources_compared.appendix_d: Bussey and Hoffman, 'Human Mars Landing Site and Impacts on Mars Surface Operations', 2016 IEEE Aerospace Conference, NTRS 20160001040, https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20160001040/downloads/20160001040.pdf, Appendix D, pages 19-20. 47 rows; Ausonia Cavus (1045) appears twice; no rows for 1016, 1018 or 1049. Its 'Longitude' column holds index numbers 1-44, not longitudes, so only latitude was compared.

not_confirmed: Which abstract the organisers left out of their '45 abstracts' (see counts.why_49_not_47).
1054 states no longitude convention; the east-positive reading rests on the named features and the NASA map.
1026: the stated centre lies near the east edge of the circle drawn in the abstract's own Figure 1 (about 50 km off); the stated value is kept.
1011a (Erebus Montes): the NASA map circle is about 10 degrees east of the stated centre; the stated centre fits the USGS extent of Erebus Montes better.
1021: the NASA map circle is about 4.8 degrees south of the stated centre; Appendix D agrees with the abstract. The abstract's words 'west of Argyre Planitia' do not fit its own numbers.
1048 (map 1.5 degrees west) and 1023 (map 1.1 degrees south) differ from the map by just over 1 degree; the abstracts' values are kept.
1030, 1049, 1051 have no position in words; 1040 has latitude only.
Zones 1006, 1009, 1015, 1022, 1023, 1027, 1035, 1037, 1045a, 1045b, 1048, 1053, 1056 give a position for the zone without calling it the centre or the landing site.
The individual workshop presentations (one PDF per talk on NASA's presentations page) were not downloaded or checked.

meta.credit: The abstracts are (c) their authors, published by the Lunar and Planetary Institute; only names, positions and one sentence of our own words are taken. Abstracts 1031 and 1056 are cited from NASA's compiled abstract set. The exploration zone map and the Final Workshop Statement are from NASA; Appendix D is from Bussey and Hoffman (2016, NTRS 20160001040). zones.authors: D. C. Barker, G. James, G. Chamitoff, S. Clifford

zones.position_kind: landing site, stated (whole degrees)
zones.region: Arcadia Planitia, along Phlegra Dorsa (northern plains)
zones.why: Ground ice fills the top tens of metres here, so crews can mine water; low dust and few rocks suit heavy landers.
zones.use_reason: Position stated in the abstract's words.
zones.note: The zone is the 100 km around this landing site. The abstract also names three higher-latitude places (49°N, 126°E; 49.5°N, 160°E; 47°N, 13°W) that 'will need to be considered' later; they are not proposed zones and are not listed. Tyndall crater (USGS Gazetteer 39.73 N, 169.97 E) lies about 100 km away, which fits the text ('just outside our 100 km EZ').

The LPI program lists this abstract (Equatorial I), but the NASA agenda v11 has no talk for it and the NASA abstract set files it as a poster.
